abstract.t: This document specifies a YANG module for discovering transport capabilities for YANG notifications. The module augments the YANG notifications capabilities model with capabilities for the notification transport protocol, transport encoding, and transport encryption. The capabilities enable a client to determine the notification transport options supported by a NETCONF or RESTCONF server at runtime or at implementation time using the YANG instance data file format.

section.title: Introduction
section.t: The "ietf-system-capabilities" YANG module defined in allows a NETCONF or RESTCONF client to discover capabilities supported by a NETCONF or RESTCONF server, including basic system capabilities and YANG-Push related capabilities. These capabilities can be provided at implementation time or reported at runtime, allowing a client to determine which YANG management features are supported by the server.

YANG Notifications, as defined in and , allow clients to establish subscriptions for receiving YANG notifications from a NETCONF or RESTCONF server. A server may support multiple notification delivery protocols, encoding formats, and security protocols. Knowledge of these capabilities can allow a client to select an appropriate notification delivery protocol and associated parameters when establishing a subscription.

Currently, a client may determine whether a particular notification delivery protocol and its associated parameters are supported only by attempting to use them through configuration. For example, a NETCONF or RESTCONF server may reject a subscription request when the requested notification delivery parameters, such as the delivery protocol, encoding format, or security protocol, are not supported. As described in , a simple negotiation mechanism, such as inserting hints into an error response to a failed RPC request, can increase the likelihood of success for subsequent RPC requests involving subscription parameters. While such error responses can help establish a subscription, they are not widely supported and may result in unexpected failures or additional message exchanges between the client and server.

This document defines a YANG module that extends the system capabilities model defined in with capabilities specific to the delivery of YANG notifications. The module allows a NETCONF or RESTCONF client to discover, from a NETCONF or RESTCONF server, the notification delivery protocols, encoding formats, and security protocols supported for YANG notifications. The capabilities can be provided at implementation time using the YANG instance data file format or discovered at runtime through a YANG management protocol.

section.title: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
The terms "subscription", "publisher", and "receiver" are used as defined in .
The terms "client", and "server" are used as defined in .
The term "transport protocol" is used as defined by the "transport" identity in and refers to the notification delivery protocol used to deliver YANG notifications between a publisher and a receiver.

section.title: Capabilities for Systems and Datastore Update Notifications
section.t: lists the NETCONF/RESTCONF server capabilities related to YANG-Push that are supported in the YANG module "ietf-notification-capabilities".
These server capabilities are transport independent, session level capabilities. They can be provided either at the implementation time or reported at runtime.
This document provides additional attributes associated with system capabilities that are related to the YANG notification delivery protocol:

list.t: Transport protocols supported for YANG notifications that a client can request when establishing a subscription. This includes HTTPS-based or UDP-based transports for configured subscriptions.
YANG notifications encoding formats supported by the NETCONF/RESTCONF server. This includes XML , JSON or CBOR .
Security protocols supported for protecting connections for YANG notifications. This includes DTLS 1.2, DTLS 1.3, TLS 1.2, and TLS 1.3.

section.t: The values advertised by these capabilities are defined using YANG identities. The set of values is therefore not limited to the identities defined or referenced by this document. The "transport-protocol" leaf uses identities derived from the "transport" identity defined in . Notification transport specifications define identities derived from this base identity for the transports they specify. For example, defines the "https" transport identity, while defines the "udp-notif" transport identity. These identities can consequently be advertised as values of the "transport-protocol" leaf.

The same mechanism is used for notification encoding formats and security protocols. The "notification-encoding-format" leaf-list uses identities derived from the "encoding" identity defined in . For example, defines the "encode-xml" and "encode-json" identities, while additional encodings can be defined by other YANG modules. Similarly, security protocol versions are represented by identities, including the TLS identities defined in and the DTLS identities defined in this document. New values can be introduced by defining new identities derived from the corresponding base identity.
The model defined in this document augments the System Capabilities model defined in .

This model is intended to be used between an orchestrator and a network device that provides YANG notifications. A management network between the orchestrator and the network device is assumed to be available for exchanging YANG management information. The management connectivity and endpoint of the network device are expected to be provisioned as part of the management network configuration. The orchestrator can use the established management connection to discover the notification transport capabilities of the network device before establishing the notification subscription.

section.t: The following tree diagram provides an overview of the data model.

section.title: Security Considerations
section.t: The "ietf-yp-transport-capabilities" YANG module defines a data model that is designed to be accessed via YANG-based management protocols, such as NETCONF and RESTCONF . These protocols have to use a secure transport layer (e.g., SSH , TLS , and QUIC ) and have to use mutual authentication.

The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) provides the means to restrict access for particular NETCONF or RESTCONF users to a preconfigured subset of all available NETCONF or RESTCONF protocol operations and content.

All protocol-accessible data nodes are read-only and cannot be modified. However, the 'transport-security-protocol' leaf-list exposes the security protocol versions supported by the server. This information can reveal aspects of the server's security posture, including support for obsolete or deprecated protocol versions, and may facilitate enumeration of the server's security capabilities. Access to this information SHOULD therefore be restricted to authorized users using appropriate access control mechanisms, such as NACM. This module inherits all the security considerations of .

section.t: In addition, the client could also query notification transport capabilities from the NETCONF or RESTCONF server. For example, the client sends <get> request message to the server to query from the server.
